When people stroke a cat under the chin while saying, “Good kitty, you’re so cute,” the cat makes a purring sound around its throat. default.p.test-1-p2.vietnamese:
As I walked past a convenience store near my home, I felt that the familiar scene somehow looked different. The reason was that the garbage bins that had always been placed in front of the store had suddenly disappeared overnight. Until the previous day, there should still have been three types of bins in front of the store: burnable garbage, bottles and cans, and plastic bottles. When I went inside and asked the manager where the garbage bins had gone,

「I moved the garbage bins from over there. If we leave them outside, many people bring household garbage and throw it away. We tried measures such as posting notices saying, 'Please do not dispose of household garbage here,' but they were ineffective, so we had no choice but to move the garbage bins inside the store.」

Convenience stores sell many items that are consumed on the spot, so they provide garbage bins to prevent litter from harming the appearance of the surrounding area. Being able to throw away garbage could be called one of the store’s customer services. Therefore, naturally, this is a service that only people who use the store’s services have the right to enjoy.

(Note 1) Appearance: a beautiful landscape or view

(Note 2) Service: attentive assistance intended to satisfy customers, without the aim of making a profit

default.p.test-10-p1.vietnamese:
There is a tree called the Nemunoki. It is said to have come to be called "Nemunoki" (sleeping tree) because its leaves close in the late afternoon, making it look as though the tree is sleeping. When the sun sets, the tree closes its leaves as if stacking them on top of one another, but the leaves close in exactly the same way even when they are artificially covered to create shade.

So why does the Nemunoki close its leaves in the late afternoon? One purpose of closing its leaves seems to be preventing water loss by shutting them. But that is not the only reason. It is thought that the tree closes its leaves in the evening because strong moonlight at night would disrupt the plant's inherent biological rhythm. The name "Nemunoki" alone sounds adorable, but learning that the tree cannot sleep when the night is bright makes it seem somewhat human and naturally gives one a feeling of closeness.

(Note 1) 親近感: a feeling of closeness or familiarity.

default.p.test-10-p2.vietnamese:
What is the meaning of studying history? Although the past can no longer be changed, is it really necessary to study it now? If we know about the past, we can understand travel destinations and novels more deeply, making those experiences more enjoyable. If so, is history merely a form of knowledge and education?

Time connects the past to the present and then moves toward the future. Without the past, there would be no present. Our society today has taken shape through the accumulation of events in the past. If so, by studying the past and learning why things happened, we may be able to understand events and problems in society today. Moreover, we may be able to predict problems that will arise in the future and find ways to deal with them. By following the successful examples of people in the past and trying not to repeat their failures, we may even be able to make the time ahead better.

default.p.test-10-p3.vietnamese:
What kind of image comes to mind when you hear the word “communication”? Perhaps some people imagine discussing something together as thoroughly as possible and eventually understanding one another. When you think of someone with good communication skills, you probably picture a person who speaks comfortably and can chat with anyone.

However, “listening” is also communication. Imagine talking to someone who gives you no response at all. Wouldn’t you find it rather difficult to continue the conversation? If you respond with comments such as “I see. What happened next?”, “Really? I had no idea!”, or “I see—you think it was ○○, right? But what about □□?”, the speaker will surely find it easier to talk. Alternatively, even without putting it into words, you can reassure the speaker by conveying that “I am listening carefully to your story,” for example by nodding along and saying “yes, yes,” or opening your eyes wide with a surprised expression. In this way, even an apparently passive action such as “listening” can clearly communicate the listener’s thoughts to the other person.

Thinking about it this way, we can say that “listening” is also an important form of communication.

(Note 1) 長けた: Excellent, outstanding, highly skilled

In the Edo period, when books were valuable and expensive, obtaining information required a great deal of money and time. In modern times, however, we can easily obtain information by searching the Internet. On the other hand, some information is unrelated to what we want to know, and some information itself is inaccurate. What we need as people living in the modern age is the ability to verify information. In a sea of information, if we cannot determine where the answer we seek is found or which information is accurate, we cannot make use of this valuable resource. default.p.test-11-p2.vietnamese:
In Japan, people commonly put their hands together and say「Itadakimasu」before beginning a meal. This is one of Japan’s customs. Some countries outside Japan also have words that are said before meals. However, their implications are slightly different from those in Japan. For example, the pre-meal expression in France, literally translated, means「good appetite」, and in terms of its implication, it is close to the Japanese expression「please help yourself」. The cook says it to the people eating, or the people eating together say it to one another, meaning “Please enjoy the meal.” These words are directed toward people who are actually present in front of them. By contrast, Japan’s「Itadakimasu」is said with gratitude to the person who prepared the meal and to the food ingredients. Gratitude toward the ingredients includes not only gratitude for the lives of animals such as meat and fish, but also gratitude toward nature and the people who grow rice and vegetables. Even when there is no one in front of them to thank, people express their gratitude by saying「Itadakimasu」. The Japanese tendency to think that they are sustained through their close relationships with people and nature is clearly expressed in the phrase「Itadakimasu」.

(Note 1) Custom: An action or behavior that has become an established daily practice.

(Note 2) Please help yourself: An honorific expression meaning「eat」or「drink」.

default.p.test-11-p3.vietnamese:
In modern times, the flow of time seems remarkably fast. Time itself should be the same as in the past or present—24 hours a day—yet it feels as though it passes very quickly. Whenever people remember that they need to give instructions to their subordinates, they immediately communicate by mobile phone. If they have a question for a business partner, they ask by email at once. Along with the convenience of being able to do something immediately, anytime and anywhere, people have also inadvertently come to demand immediate replies and immediate action. As a result, modern people cannot help feeling as though they are constantly being chased by time. Is it really a good thing to be swept along by busyness and simply let the days and months pass by?

When we pass through a street by car, we may speed past without noticing newly opened shops. This is because when people move faster than a certain speed, their field of vision becomes narrower. However, even on the same street, if we stroll through it leisurely, we can make new discoveries, such as realizing, “Oh, there is a new shop in a place like this.”

In the same way, if we are swept along by busyness and let the days and months fly by, will our field of vision not become narrower, preventing us from making new discoveries? From time to time, we should try having days when we slow down a little. By spending time leisurely, we will surely be able to make new discoveries.

(Note 1) Field of vision (視野): The range that can be seen.

default.p.test-12-p1.vietnamese:
A
This was my first time attending the「Parent-and-Child Classical Concert」. Classical concerts usually have age restrictions, so it is not possible to enjoy them with young children. This time, I brought my two sons, aged 4 and 2, but I did not have to worry about bothering the people around us even when they made a little noise, and I was able to enjoy the music fully. The only slight disappointment was that, since the concert began at 7 p.m., my children were sleepy by the time we went home. It would have been nice if it had been held during the day.

B
Thank you very much for the wonderful performance. I have attended the「Parent-and-Child Classical Concert」for three consecutive years, and each time the program is different, so I can always enjoy it with a fresh feeling. This time, my child reacted enthusiastically to a piece they had heard in a television commercial. Since my child is older and busy with extracurricular activities during the day, the evening start time was very convenient. I sincerely hope to attend again next year.

Questioner A

I am having a very hard time because I often forget things. Although I rarely experience a major failure because I forgot something, I often leave behind things I need, which is very inconvenient. Recently, I forgot my university library card and could not enter the library, and I left my umbrella on a train and had to walk home soaking wet in the rain. When I consciously remind myself not to forget something, everything is fine, but as soon as I relax and let my attention slip, I leave something behind again. For things I absolutely must not forget, I have made a list of what to bring and posted it on the wall, so I rarely forget them. Besides this method, please tell me if there are any other effective measures.

Respondent B

The way you forget things can be divided into two types. One is forgetting to take something with you, and the other is forgetting to bring something back.

When you forget to take something with you, it is better to designate one place and keep all the things you usually take with you there. When you go out, you can simply take the things from that place and leave. This also saves you the trouble of searching everywhere.

On the other hand, when you forget to bring something back, you should look back once before leaving and check what belongings you have with you. Saying aloud the things you need to take back while checking them is also very effective. By saying them aloud, you can check more carefully than if you only checked them in your head.

Times when you are moving, such as leaving your home or getting up from your seat, are the key moments when you need to pay attention. Please give these methods a try.

default.p.test-13-p1.vietnamese:
An area of sea deeper than 200 meters is called ①the deep sea. The deep-sea fish that live in these waters are known to have undergone unique evolutionary processes.

First of all, one major characteristic of the deep sea is that light has more difficulty reaching it than shallower waters, and the water temperature is low. For this reason, the fish living there have bodies capable of enduring low water temperatures.

In addition, because there are few nutrients, another characteristic of the deep sea is the small number of organisms themselves. This means that not only are opportunities for males and females of the same species to encounter each other and reproduce very limited, but opportunities to encounter prey and eat in order to survive are also extremely rare.

Even under such circumstances, ②deep-sea organisms adjust their bodies to suit their environment and survive. For example, some fish can make their stomachs swell to a size larger than their own bodies. In an environment where opportunities to encounter other fish are scarce, these fish have become capable of swallowing even large fish whole so as not to waste any small opportunity.

In this way, fish living in the deep sea have spent many years evolving into their present forms according to their needs, so that they can continue living even in this harsh environment (Note 1).

(Note 1) Harsh: extremely severe or difficult conditions

default.p.test-13-p2.vietnamese:
Japan is home to many different kinds of insects. Among them, there are quite a few rare species. The Maimaikaburi beetle is one such species. So, in what ways is the Maimaikaburi beetle unusual?

First, the Maimaikaburi beetle can be considered unusual because it is endemic to Japan, meaning that it lives only in Japan. Moreover, even when people try to search for similar insects, none can be found outside Japan.

It can also be considered unusual because its main food is maimai, or land snails. However, although it uses snails as prey, it does not eat the shell at all. It eats only the snail's flesh inside the shell. At this point, because the Maimaikaburi beetle thrusts its head inside the snail's shell, from the outside it looks exactly as though it is wearing the shell on its head. This is said to be why it was given the name 「Maimaikaburi」.

Furthermore, the fact that its color and shape vary considerably from region to region can also be regarded as an unusual characteristic. This is thought to be because the Maimaikaburi beetle's wings have degenerated, leaving it unable to fly. In other words, because it cannot fly, it cannot travel long distances, and it is thought to have diverged independently in each region.

(Note 1) Katatsumuri: a terrestrial spiral-shelled mollusk (land snail)

(Note 2) Kaigara: the hard outer covering of a snail or shellfish (shell)

(Note 3) Taika: a phenomenon in which an organ of a living organism deteriorates, becomes smaller, or disappears completely (degeneration)

(Note 4) Bunka: the separation into various forms or types during development (divergence)

default.p.test-14-p1.vietnamese:
When you act, do you really think things through for yourself before taking action? Some opinions will probably be heard, such as:「Isn't that obvious?」「What are you talking about?」「What else could we do?」.

However, is that really the truth?

Here, I would like to introduce an example observed by Fabre (Note 1), a man born in France in the 19th century, involving a species of digger wasp. Species in the digger-wasp family use their stingers to anesthetize (Note 3) insects, rendering them unable to move. They then carry the insect back to their nest, lay eggs on it, turn it into food for the newly hatched larvae, and seal the entrance to the nest from the outside with soil.

Suppose someone removed the insect from the nest right in front of a wasp that was in the process of sealing the entrance with soil. What would happen?

In reality, nothing would happen. Even if the insect were removed from the nest right before its eyes, the wasp would continue sealing the nest. The reason it continues sealing the nest is that it is not thinking and acting independently; it is merely carrying out a predetermined action in a predetermined sequence, like an instinct.

Now, let us relate this to human behavior and think about it. Have you ever acted without thinking for yourself, saying something like:「Because it is a rule」or「Because there is no other way」? Human beings are creatures capable of making their own judgments and taking action. Let us develop the habit of thinking through the reasons ourselves before acting, rather than being swept along by other people or by the information around us.

(Note 1) Fabre: a French zoologist

(Note 2) Anabachi: a species of wasp that digs holes in the ground to build its nest

(Note 3) Anesthetize: to use a drug to paralyze the nerves so that pain is not felt

default.p.test-14-p2.vietnamese:
In Japan, dried persimmons have been made since ancient times. There are sweet persimmons and astringent persimmons. Sweet persimmons can be eaten immediately after being harvested. Astringent persimmons, on the other hand, look exactly like sweet persimmons, but taste completely different and have a noticeable bitterness, so they cannot be eaten as they are. Dried persimmons are made by drying astringent persimmons in the sun so that they can be eaten.

The substance that causes persimmons to taste bitter is water-soluble tannin (Notes 1 and 2). Sweet persimmons contain little water-soluble tannin, or during ripening (Note 3), the tannin changes into an insoluble form (Note 4), so they are hardly bitter. Astringent persimmons, however, contain a great deal of water-soluble tannin. When eaten, this tannin dissolves in saliva, making the bitterness clearly noticeable on the tongue. By peeling astringent persimmons and drying the flesh, the tannin changes into an insoluble state. As a result, the bitterness can no longer be tasted, and the fruit's natural sweetness becomes noticeable.

Dried persimmons have the advantages of being sweeter than fresh persimmons and being suitable for long-term storage. In the past, when sweets made with sugar were extremely precious, dried persimmons were a highly valued snack. Recently, the traditional method of skillfully using the natural environment to make dried persimmons has once again received recognition. It is hoped that these traditional techniques and wisdom will be continued and passed down.

(Note 1) Water solubility: the property of dissolving in water

(Note 2) Tannin: a substance also used in writing ink...

(Note 3) Ripening: the process by which fruit becomes fully ripe and juicy

(Note 4) Insolubility: the property of not dissolving in a liquid

default.p.test-15-p1.vietnamese:
The moment you take one step outside your home, you are in a public place. Examples of problematic behavior in such places include sitting on the ground in front of a convenience store to eat, drink, or chat. Even though it may not involve making a lot of noise, it somehow still makes the people around them feel uncomfortable.

Applying makeup while seated on a train is similar. Although it is not necessarily prohibited in that location, it is behavior that people do not consider appropriate there. Those around the person may find it strange, feel uncomfortable and wonder whether such behavior is acceptable, or feel overwhelmed by someone who can act so casually in this way.

In public places, we need to be aware of how our behavior appears to those around us. We should think before acting so that everyone present can spend their time pleasantly and comfortably.

default.p.test-15-p2.outline.4.label: Vocabulary notes in the passage
default.p.test-15-p2.outline.4.note: Explains terms appearing in the passage: produce in season (旬) and a vinyl-covered agricultural greenhouse (ビニールハウス).
default.p.test-15-p2.vietnamese:
All vegetables and fruits have a "peak season."

Take mandarins, for example. Because their peak season is winter, when winter arrives, fragrant and delicious mandarins are packed in cardboard boxes and sold cheaply. However, ①mandarins can still be bought in summer. This is because they are grown in special environments such as vinyl greenhouses covered with plastic sheeting. However, the fruit is small and its color is still green. In terms of taste, it probably cannot compare at all with mandarins in peak season. Moreover, it costs several times more than during the peak season, when the price is lowest. It is indeed a somewhat premium product.

②When eating vegetables or fruit, those in their peak season are undoubtedly the best choice. Precisely because supermarkets now make it easy to buy almost anything at any time, it has become even more important to know the peak season of each vegetable and fruit.

(Note 1) Peak season (shun): the period when something can be eaten fresher and more deliciously than at other times.

(Note 2) Vinyl greenhouse: an agricultural greenhouse covered with vinyl sheeting.

default.p.test-16-p1.outline.0.label: Introduction to the two ways of calculating age in Japan
default.p.test-16-p1.outline.0.note: Raises the question of whether a newborn baby is 0 or 1 year old and introduces Japan’s two age-counting systems: full age (満年齢) and traditional age (数え年).
default.p.test-16-p1.outline.1.label: How exact age and traditional age are calculated
default.p.test-16-p1.outline.1.note: The passage explains and compares the calculation of completed age, based on the date of birth, and traditional East Asian age, in which a person starts at age 1 and gains another year at New Year. This supports the answer to Question 1.
default.p.test-16-p1.outline.2.label: The popularity of milestone ages in modern life
default.p.test-16-p1.outline.2.note: Clearly states that official documents and everyday communication are increasingly using completed age rather than traditional age reckoning to avoid misunderstandings.
default.p.test-16-p1.outline.3.label: Traditional occasions that still use traditional age reckoning
default.p.test-16-p1.outline.3.note: Explains that the traditional practice of counting age inclusively at birth is still passed down and used in traditional events such as Shichigosan for children and celebrations for older people. Provides evidence for Question 2.
default.p.test-16-p1.vietnamese:
How old is a baby who has just been born? Many people might answer “0 years old,” but saying “1 year old” is not necessarily wrong. In Japan, there are two ways to count age: “completed age” and “traditional age.”

With “completed age,” you add one year every time your birthday comes around. A newborn baby is 0 years old. “Traditional age,” on the other hand, considers a person to be 1 year old in the year they are born. Therefore, a newborn baby is 1 year old. Then, one year is added every New Year's Day (January 1).

“Traditional age” was common in the past, but today people use “completed age.” When filling out official documents or introducing yourself, you should state your completed age. This will probably prevent misunderstandings. However, traditional age is also an old Japanese custom that has been passed down through the years, and it is still used today. It seems that traditional age is often used for events such as Shichigosan, which celebrates children reaching the ages of 7, 5, and 3, and for celebrations of the longevity of elderly people.

default.p.test-18-p1.vietnamese:
At a nearby park, a large number of elderly people had gathered. When I asked about it, I learned that a Ground Golf tournament was taking place. I thought it was a sport I had never heard of, but apparently it is considered a “new sport.” New sports are sports that have been newly created, and most of them seem to have the characteristic that anyone can enjoy them easily and casually.

At a community gathering held at a nearby junior high school, Kin-Ball was introduced. Kin-Ball is a large, soft ball more than 1 meter in diameter that can be used to play simple games. I heard that competitive sports such as volleyball can also be played with it, but with games like Kin-Ball, whose rules are as simple as passing the ball and keeping it from falling, people of many different ages, from children to the elderly, can play safely.

It is often said that in modern society, the ties between people are becoming increasingly weak. Saying that sports can “deepen interaction” may sound rather grand, but new sports may be just the right thing to try casually. Wouldn’t gathering elderly people together, or people from different generations, and trying a new sport with the attitude of “Why not give it a try?” provide an opportunity to build stronger ties among local residents?

default.p.test-18-p2.outline.3.label: The author’s central view on selling books
default.p.test-18-p2.outline.3.note: In the conclusion and note, the author asserts that a book's core is its content. Rather than spending effort beautifying the exterior, one should focus on communicating the content to attract genuine readers. Question 2 is mainly based on this passage.
default.p.test-18-p2.vietnamese:
When I go to the paperback section of a bookstore, sometimes the book cover catches my eye more than the title does. Some covers feature photos like those in celebrity magazines, while others use manga-style illustrations. Yet the books themselves are works of literature.

In music, there is a practice known as “buying by the cover” (choosing a record based on its packaging design rather than its content, such as the artist or songs). Could they be aiming for something like that? However, I also have the impression that people who “buy by the cover” when purchasing records tend to be fairly avid music listeners. They do it with a playful attitude, thinking, “Let’s try listening to something I don’t know much about for a change.” Sometimes they will discover a great song, and sometimes they will end up with a terrible record. They already anticipate and accept that possibility.

On the other hand, I do not think that people who intend to “buy by the cover” when choosing paperbacks are necessarily avid readers. Since they are looking at books in a bookstore, they are probably thinking, “I’ll try reading something.” When they are wondering, “Which book should I read now?”, the cover design is likely to become one of the factors that makes them pick up a book. Yet no matter how appealing the cover may be, will people really want to buy the book and try reading it without caring about the content at all? Even if they buy a book that way and end up disappointed, will they continue buying books?

It is certainly true that books with eye-catching designs sell well right away. In the end, however, what remains is the content of the book. Wouldn’t making an effort to explore ways of conveying that content, instead of devoting all our energy to polishing the outward appearance, increase the number of genuine readers?

（注1）承知の上: Knowing this but accepting it anyway.

default.p.test-19-p1.outline.2.note: The author advises that if something concerns you, do not use being busy as an excuse; make time to try it, change course if it goes wrong, and discover what you truly want to do through repeated experience. Provides the basis for Question 1.
default.p.test-19-p1.vietnamese:
I often hear people complain, "I do not know what I really want to do." As a result, whether choosing a school or looking for a job, they have neither a firm aspiration nor a clear direction for the future, so things cannot go smoothly. Some people blame social circumstances or those around them for their lack of progress and set off on a journey to find themselves. Perhaps the reason they do not know what they like or what they could pursue so passionately that they would lose track of time is that, during their school years, they never had enough time to think about such things.

There probably are not many people who clearly know which path they should take immediately after graduating from junior high or high school. Quite a few people believe they have made up their minds to go on to university or a vocational school, but when they actually study specialized subjects, they feel that things are different from what they had imagined. In a life where one simply devotes all one's energy to dealing with the tasks at hand without knowing whether one is interested in them, how can there be enough time and peace of mind to think carefully about what one loves? Then, when the time comes and one is pressured to make a decision, it is difficult to arrive at a satisfactory answer even by thinking frantically.

Therefore, if there is something on your mind, do not use your daily busyness as an excuse; try setting aside a certain amount of time for it. If it does not suit you, there is nothing wrong with moving on to the next thing. I believe that what we truly want to do can only be discovered through the gradual accumulation of experiences like these.

May 10, 20XX

Dear Mr. Eric Wilson,

Joy Joy Kids Children's English Class

Center Director: Mayumi Asakawa

Seasonal greetings: As summer approaches, I hope you are in increasingly good health and that your work continues to prosper.

When our center was established last year, you gave us tremendous assistance. We would like to express our sincere gratitude.

We have now decided to hold a “Summer Camp” for our students. The camp is scheduled to take place for three days and two nights in early August at a nearby campground. We are therefore contacting you to ask whether you would be willing to serve as an instructor at this camp.

You have participated in our center's events many times before, and all of our staff are extremely grateful to you. The students and their parents have greatly appreciated your enthusiastic instruction, and many have earnestly requested that we invite you to be an instructor this time. We know that you are very busy, but we would be delighted if you would kindly consider our request.

Sincerely,

default.p.test-2-p1.outline.2.note: Explains that 80% of cherry trees are Somei Yoshino, propagated clonally by grafting or cuttings. They therefore have identical structures, like a single tree, and bloom simultaneously under the same weather conditions.

default.p.test-2-p1.vietnamese:
Whenever spring arrives, we hear the term "cherry blossom front" in weather forecasts. The "cherry blossom front" is a line connecting the dates when cherry blossoms bloom across Japan, and it is usually shown on a map like a weather chart. In general, this front moves from south to north and from lower elevations to higher ones. Yet this is an extremely strange phenomenon. Even among flowers that bloom in spring, other species, such as azaleas and dandelions, never bloom all at once in the same area. Not only azaleas and dandelions, but also flowers other than cherry blossoms bloom at different times from tree to tree and flower to flower, even in the same area. For this reason, it is impossible to set a blooming date for each area and connect the dates with lines like the "cherry blossom front." However, cherry blossoms in the same area bloom all at once at the same time. ①Why does this difference occur?

Eighty percent of Japan’s cherry trees belong to the Somei Yoshino variety. Somei Yoshino cherry trees throughout the country are propagated through methods such as grafting (Note 1) and cuttings (Note 2). Grafting and taking cuttings reproduce exact clones of the original parent tree, so all the trees have exactly the same structure. In other words, all the Somei Yoshino trees in Japan can be regarded as one single tree. ②Consequently, in neighboring areas with similar blooming conditions, such as similar temperatures, the cherry blossoms bloom all at once, making it possible to connect the blooming dates into lines called the "cherry blossom front."

(Note 1) Grafting: A method of propagation in which a branch from one tree is grafted onto another tree.

(Note 2) Taking cuttings: A method of propagation in which a branch is inserted into soil so that it takes root.

May 18, 20XX

Dear Ms. Sara Aoki

Hamakami Ginza Shopping District Association
Chairman Masao Ueda

Dear Ms. Aoki,

The season of fresh green leaves has arrived, stretching as far as the eye can see. I trust that you continue to be active and successful.

Although you are busy, we are delighted that you and everyone in your dance class have agreed to perform on stage at the Shopping District Association's Autumn Festival. We sincerely thank you.

Sincerely,

default.p.test-21-p1.vietnamese:
Recently, efforts to cover elementary and junior high school grounds with grass have been gaining momentum. Grass-covered school grounds offer many benefits. First, students can run and play freely. This is because grass is much softer than traditional dirt, so children do not have to worry as much about getting hurt when they fall. In addition, grass helps lower the ground temperature in summer. On dirt grounds, dust can fill the air when the surface dries out, interfering with physical activity, but this does not happen on grass. The fresh green color of the grass also seems to brighten the spirits of students who spend much of their time at school.

It is said that once a school ground becomes a lawn, opportunities to interact with students in other grades also arise. This is because more students voluntarily go outside to exercise during recess. Furthermore, this may help improve their physical fitness. For children's physical and emotional development, the role of a grassy school ground seems to be very significant.

default.p.test-22-p1.outline.5.note: Explaining 人一倍 (far more than the average person).
default.p.test-22-p1.vietnamese:
Once you get used to it, it may not seem like a big deal, but many people feel that speaking in front of an audience is one of their weaknesses.

If you begin something while thinking, "This is so boring because I'm not good at it," it will rarely go smoothly. Perhaps this is because you fall into an attitude of giving up, thinking, "It won't go well anyway." Conversely, if you begin with the thought, "I will work hard to overcome this weakness," you may often achieve satisfactory results.

One person, wanting to overcome an inferiority complex about being poor at speaking in front of an audience, volunteered to chair meetings. Apparently, this person prepared twice as thoroughly as the average person before taking part each time, and after a year no longer felt inadequate at public speaking.

When taking on things we are not good at, we must make an effort. As we work hard to carry them out, our own problems will surely become clear, and there may be times when we feel like running away. It becomes necessary to overcome that barrier.

For this reason, when it comes to things we are weak at, we should actively challenge ourselves with a positive attitude. Since we already feel that we are not good at them, we can begin with the mindset that failure is only natural. We should keep persevering until we achieve the satisfying feeling that we have completed the task and done our very best. If we do so, it will surely become an experience that leads to our own personal growth.

(Note 1) Far surpassing others: Being considerably better than the average person.

August 1, 20XX

Hearty Net Co., Ltd.

Dear Mr. Adam Johnson

Jurakusha Co., Ltd.

Minoru Tagawa

Dear Sir or Madam,

In this intensely hot late-summer weather, I sincerely hope that everyone at your company remains in excellent health and that your company continues to prosper.

I was delighted to learn that your company is celebrating its 25th anniversary, and I would like to offer my heartfelt congratulations.

I would also like to sincerely thank you for inviting me to the anniversary celebration on October 3.

Under normal circumstances, I should have visited you in person first to offer my congratulations. Unfortunately, I already have an appointment that day and will be unable to attend. I sincerely apologize from the bottom of my heart for this discourtesy.

I would also like to send your company a small congratulatory gift.

I sincerely hope that the anniversary celebration will be a great success, and I also hope that our companies will continue to maintain our excellent relationship in the years ahead.

Yours sincerely,

default.p.test-27-p3.vietnamese:
Osaka City, homemaker (34)

On sunny days, I often take my two-year-old son to play in a park near our home. The flowers and plants in the park are carefully maintained, and every time I visit, I feel refreshed.

However, for about a month now, the garbage bins in this park have often been overflowing. Empty cans and plastic bottles are being thrown into the bin for burnable garbage, and the waste is not being sorted, completely ruining the beautiful scenery. In addition, crows and cats rummage through kitchen waste brought from people's homes, making the area extremely unsanitary.

Since the users' lack of awareness continues, why not decisively try removing the garbage bins altogether? Some people may say, 「 ① Without garbage bins, it would be inconvenient 」. However, wouldn't it be enough for each person to take responsibility and take their own garbage home?

I sincerely hope that the park management will consider this matter so that the park can become a place where everyone can spend time comfortably.

(Note 1) 撤去 (removal): the act of taking something away.

(Note 2) 清々しい (refreshing): fresh and pleasant.

(Note 3) 分別 (sorting): separating things according to type.

From: General Affairs Department - Yukari Sugita
To: [All Employees]
Subject: Notice of Evacuation Drill

Dear all,

This is to announce this year’s evacuation drill, as described below.

1. Date and time: Thursday, September 1, 20XX, 13:00 ~ 13:30
2. Drill content: A simulated evacuation drill in the event of a fire (※ The fire is assumed to have started in the employee cafeteria.)
3. Important points: Each person should check in advance the evacuation manual provided in each department. On the day of the drill, follow the instructions of the disaster-prevention staff.
・An emergency alarm will sound, followed by an internal announcement ordering an evacuation. When the announcement is made, begin evacuating promptly.
・The evacuation site is the official parking lot north of the head office.
・Do not use the elevators. In addition, since the simulated fire is in the employee cafeteria, please use the emergency stairs or central stairs, not the east stairs.
・In each department, the department head should check the number of employees present and report it to the disaster-prevention staff.

If anything is unclear, please contact the General Affairs Department.
Thank you for your cooperation.

====================================
General Affairs Department - Yukari Sugita
sugita-y@abc.def.co.jp　Extension 22143
====================================

default.p.test-3-p1.vietnamese:
The development of the internet in recent years has been astonishing. Almost everything—from the latest news and songs by our favorite artists to things that slightly concern us—can be found instantly by searching on the smartphone in our hands. So, is the internet all-powerful? I do not think so. (Because) the internet only shows us things that we search for ourselves. The online world seems very vast, but the world we actually come into contact with is narrower than we think. Many of the “friends” connected to us on social media probably also share certain things in common with us. We need to recognize that what we call information obtained on the internet is actually information that has already passed through the filter of our own minds.

（注1）瞬時 (instant): an extremely short period of time.

（注2）万能 (all-purpose): useful and effective for every kind of task.

（注3）フィルター (filter): a device that allows things meeting certain conditions to pass through or prevents them from passing through.

default.p.test-3-p2.outline.0.note: Opening of the reading: introduces the sparrow as a common, familiar bird since ancient times that appears frequently in traditional Japanese cultural products.

default.p.test-3-p2.outline.1.note: Shifts the discussion by describing the sudden decline in sparrow numbers over the past 20 years, along with hypotheses about food and nesting sites and the fact that the cause remains unclear. Question 2 is based mainly here.

default.p.test-3-p2.vietnamese:
Sparrows have been common birds in Japan since ancient times, and seeing them perched on telephone wires was once a familiar sight. Among traditional Japanese cultural works such as paintings and haiku, there are also many works featuring sparrows.

However, their population is said to have declined sharply over the past 20 years. The possible causes include the decrease in farmland, vacant lots, grasslands, and wooden houses, which has reduced both their food sources and nesting places. However, the cause of this decline has not yet been clarified.

In contrast, the population of crows is increasing rapidly. The crows commonly seen in Japan originally built nests by assembling branches in tall trees, but they can also build nests on high-rise buildings and steel towers. Furthermore, crows are omnivorous and feed on organic waste discarded by humans, so finding food is easy and they can live in cities. In short, the increase in crows can be said to be a result of human actions coming back to affect us.

(Note 1) ありふれた: Common; something that can be found anywhere

(Note 2) 高層ビル: A high-rise building

(Note 3) 雑食性: The characteristic of eating both animals and plants; omnivorousness

Health checkup: 8:30 a.m., Wednesday, July 11

Thank you sincerely for your continued support of the North Theater Company.
Your membership expires on August 31.
As your membership expiration date approaches, we are sending you information about the renewal procedure.

● Membership Fee
・Annual membership fee: 4,000 yen

● Renewal Procedure
・Renewal can be completed from three months before until one month after the membership expiration date.
・If you wish to renew, please use the enclosed payment slip and pay the annual membership fee at a post office before the expiration date.
・Members who complete the renewal procedure will receive a renewal commemorative gift enclosed with the next members’ newsletter.

● Important Notes
・If more than one month passes after the membership expiration date, your membership will be automatically canceled. In that case, your membership number and membership card, which you have used until now, will become invalid.
・We do not accept payments sent by cash-registered mail or ordinary mail under any circumstances. Please use the enclosed payment slip and make the payment at a post office. Payment cannot be made through a bank.
・Please be careful not to omit your address, name, telephone number, or membership number.
・Payments cannot be canceled after they have been made.

North Theater Company Fan Club Office

（Note 1）失効: becoming invalid; losing validity

（Note 2）現金書留: registered mail for sending cash

If you notice that your electronic money card, the 「MAKA Card」, has been lost or stolen, contact the Card Center immediately to request that the card be blocked. The Card Center operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. By completing the required procedures, you can transfer your balance and accumulated points to a new MAKA Card.

● Procedure from blocking the card to issuing a replacement

(1) Blocking the card and issuing a transfer code by telephone
The cardholder must contact the Card Center personally. We will issue a transfer code.
Phone: 0120-XXX-XXXX (24 hours a day, 365 days a year)

(2) Issuing a new MAKA Card
At the service counter, please give the transfer code to a staff member. We will provide you with a Transfer Application and a new MAKA Card.
【Required items】
・Transfer code

(3) Submitting the application and documents
Fill in all the required information on the Transfer Application and mail it together with a copy of an identification document.
【Required items】
・Transfer Application
・Copy of an identification document

(4) Transferring the balance
After the Transfer Application arrives at the Card Center, the electronic money balance will be transferred to the new MAKA Card within approximately 10 days.

（Note 1）Transfer (hikitsugu): to transfer something from the previous one to the next one

default.p.test-32-p2.vietnamese:
Uses and effects
Prevents and relieves dizziness, nausea, and headaches caused by motion sickness.

Directions and dosage
Take the medicine 30 minutes before boarding a vehicle or vessel, or when you experience motion sickness.

Warnings
1. The following people must not take this medicine:
① People who have previously experienced an allergic reaction to this medicine or any of its ingredients.
② Children under 4 years of age.
2. After taking this medicine, do not drive or operate vehicles or machinery.
3. Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.
4. Store out of the reach of young children.

(Note 1) Motion sickness: A condition in which you feel unwell while traveling in a vehicle or vessel.

default.p.test-32-p3.vietnamese:
Instructions

① Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces; peel the onion and slice it to a thickness of 3 mm; roughly chop the mitsuba.

② Put the chicken thighs and onion into a small pan, add the pre-mixed seasonings A, bring to a rolling boil, then cook over medium heat until done.

③ Turn the heat to high, then pour the beaten egg evenly over the ingredients.

④ Turn off the heat, cover the pan, and let it steam for about 1 to 2 minutes.

⑤ Place the filling from step ④ on top of the rice, then sprinkle the mitsuba over the top.

（Note 1） Mitsuba: a leafy vegetable

（Note 2） Zakugiri: roughly and quickly cutting ingredients into approximately sized pieces

（Note 3） Beaten egg: raw chicken eggs stirred after cracking the shells so that the yolks and whites are mixed together.

default.p.test-33-p1.vietnamese:
Hamsters are a type of rodent. They have cheek pouches that can expand.

Housing environment
・Hamsters have a very strong sense of territoriality, so if several are kept in the same cage, they will fight. Keep only one hamster in each cage.
・The appropriate room temperature for keeping hamsters is 20–24 degrees. If the temperature falls below 5 degrees, they may die. In winter, be sure to take measures to protect them from the cold.
・Place the cage somewhere away from direct sunlight and from air blowing directly from an air conditioner.

Food
・Change the water every day.
・Special hamster food is sold at pet stores, but the following foods are also acceptable.
● Foods that may be given
Carrots, pumpkin, sweet potatoes, cabbage, etc.
● Foods that may be given, but not in excessive amounts
Cucumber, tomatoes, sunflower seeds, walnuts, etc.
● Foods that must not be given
Onions, chocolate, acorns, garlic, etc.

Other
・Hamsters are nocturnal animals, so arrange playtime and care from evening through nighttime.

（注釈 1）Cheek pouch: a pouch in the cheek of animals such as squirrels, used to store food and other items.

（注釈 2）Sense of territoriality: an awareness of one’s own territory.

（注釈 3）Cage: here, a cage, basket, or similar item used for keeping hamsters.

At MM Company, to ensure that customers can shop with confidence, we accept exchanges or returns if you are dissatisfied with a product.

【Exchange and Return Procedures】

・After filling out the exchange/return form, please send it back together with the product.

・For a return, please circle one reason from the list of return reasons. For an exchange, please accurately write the size you wish to exchange it for.

・Please return the product using a home-delivery service with the recipient paying the shipping charges.

【Refund Procedures】

(1) If payment has not been made

If you return the product, you do not need to pay for it. Please cancel the payment slip currently in your possession.

We will enclose a new payment slip with the replacement product, so please make the payment using that slip.

(2) If payment has been made

Whether you are returning or exchanging the product, please provide the bank branch name and account number for the refund. The refund account must be in your own name.

In the case of an exchange, the original payment will also be refunded first. We will then send the replacement product together with a new payment slip, so please make the payment again using that slip.

（Note 1）Cash on delivery: a method of sending mail or goods in which the recipient pays the shipping charges.

20XX年6月14日

To all residents of Elegance Apartments

Elegance Apartments Management Committee

Recently, the management committee has received many complaints concerning garbage. We ask all residents to review their garbage-disposal practices and follow the rules carefully.

● Please put out your garbage before 8:00 a.m. on the designated collection day. Do not put it out the night before.

● Please follow the rules of ○○ City and sort your garbage carefully. We have seen many cases in which non-burnable garbage (Note 1) has been mixed with burnable garbage (Note 2).

● Oversized garbage (Note 3) will not be collected as regular garbage. Please check the city of ○○’s bulletin or website and dispose of it according to the designated procedure. (A fee will be charged for this service.)

〈○○ City Garbage Collection Schedule〉
・Burnable garbage: Every Monday and Thursday
・Recyclable garbage (Note 4): The first and third Wednesdays of each month
・Non-burnable garbage: The second Tuesday of each month

（Note 1）Non-burnable garbage: Garbage that cannot be burned, such as glass, ceramics, and metal parts

（Note 2）Burnable garbage: Garbage that can be burned

（Note 3）Oversized garbage: Large items such as futons and furniture

（Note 4）Recyclable garbage: Garbage that can be recycled, such as old newspapers, old magazines, and aluminum cans

default.p.test-36-p2.vietnamese:
Everyone wants to eat delicious food. Isn’t that a desire shared by all humanity? I am a self-professed food lover, and everyone around me recognizes it; whenever I hear that there is delicious food somewhere, I become restless with excitement. It would not be an exaggeration to say that in Japan, especially Tokyo, you can enjoy food from almost every part of the world. There is Japanese cuisine arranged on the plate as delicately as a work of art, French cuisine with carefully prepared sauces and complex flavors, and stylish Italian food that is perfect for a date. For a large group meal, it is hard to pass up Chinese food served on large plates, while when you are tired, Thai or Vietnamese food with its distinctive aromas and spices is also wonderful.

However, what I sometimes suddenly crave is the bowl of miso soup my mother makes. Sometimes it contains vegetables cooked until tender, and sometimes tofu and green onions. Although it is just an ordinary bowl of miso soup with nothing special about it, I can never reproduce that flavor, even when I make it myself. It is truly strange.

（Note 1）食いしん坊 (glutton, food lover): Always having an excessive desire to eat.

（Note 2）過言ではない (not an exaggeration): Not an overstatement.

（Note 3）繊細な (delicate): Detailed and carefully refined.

（Note 4）なんということのない (ordinary): Having nothing particularly special or unusual about it.

default.p.test-37-p1.vietnamese:
A little while ago, when I said to a friend, “I'm hungry. Shall we go get something to eat before we go home? How about something sweet?”, my friend once replied, “Something sweet is a little①……” I wondered what words would follow and waited, but my friend did not say anything more.

Come to think of it, some time ago my husband said, “It's about time we cleaned up,” and started cleaning. While I watched him clean and sat drinking tea, he once said to me, “It isn't just my job—why don't you help clean up too?” Apparently, the true meaning of what my husband said was not “(I) should clean up, shouldn't I?” but “Let's clean up together.”

Instead of clearly stating what they are thinking, Japanese people use vague expressions. This really made me think, “That is so typically Japanese,” but if possible, I would like the other person to communicate clearly what they are thinking from the beginning.

(Note 1) あいまい: A state in which something is unclear or vague.

default.p.test-37-p2.vietnamese:
My close friend from high school runs a cake shop in her hometown. It is a fairly well-known shop that now has two branches in the city, and I hear that it sometimes opens temporary stalls in shopping centers as well. Whenever I happen to stop by, I see her working energetically; she has loved making sweets since she was a high school student.

I once ate an extremely hard, bitter coffee-flavored cookie she made while experimenting. Even now, whenever we meet, I tease her by saying things like, “That cookie was so hard it almost broke my teeth,” although it was not really that hard. But it was hard, all right.

To avoid any misunderstanding, let me make it clear that the sweets she made back then were already delicious. The things she baked for me included not only cookies but also many other varieties, such as soft, fluffy rolled cakes. Nevertheless, what remains in my memory after several decades is the hardness and slightly bitter taste of the innovative cookie made by kneading instant coffee into the dough and baking it. It is difficult to call it “delicious.” Yet I do not feel at all like saying that it was “not delicious.”

If I could cross space and time and return to an ordinary afternoon during those high school days, I would still want to eat that cookie.

（Note 1）Local area: The place where a person lives

（Note 2）Imaya: Now, at present

（Note 3）Tōtei: No matter what, absolutely (not)

default.p.test-37-p3.vietnamese:
On a holiday morning, I am not awakened by the sound of an alarm clock; I get up after naturally opening my eyes. I open the curtains to let in the sunlight, turn on my favorite music, and drink coffee. Should I choose J.S. Bach or Debussy today? I make such a happy choice and let myself sink into the pleasant flow of music. I tell myself how precious moments like these are. They are truly joyful and relaxing moments.

Things were not like this in the past, when I was determined to make a living through music. What should the performance style of Baroque music be like? What do the markings in the score indicate? What were the composer's intentions? I would stare at the score and analyze it. When friends told me, "You are trying to turn what you like into a job, aren't you?" I wondered whether I really loved music. Gradually, no matter how many times I thought about it, I could not find an answer. Music was inseparable from my life then, yet it also persistently clung to me.

Now I have a job unrelated to music. Although it is not the work I had always dreamed of, I still listen to the music I have loved since then. No longer tormented by interpreting how it should be performed, I simply immerse myself in the wonderful music and free my soul with thoughts such as, "How beautiful that resonance is; how gentle those sounds are." From time to time, I go to a concert hall. There I see people who have devoted themselves to the path of music—the path I once abandoned. I wonder what kind of performance today's artist will give. As I look through the program booklet, my thoughts turn to that person's entire life.

Now that I can let go of the pressure and enjoy music, I feel that music is no longer an enemy I must confront, but rather a kindred friend who is always there to share my feelings.

(Note 1) J.S. Bach: A German composer active in the 18th century

(Note 2) Debussy: A French composer active from the late 19th to the early 20th century

(Note 3) 身を立てる: to make a living, sustain oneself

(Note 4) Baroque: A European musical style from the late 16th to the mid-18th century

(Note 5) 音楽の道: A professional career in music

(Note 6) 思いをはせる: to direct one's thoughts and feelings toward something

The manager called out Shuichi’s finishing time as he crossed the finish line of the 1,000-meter race. It was far slower than his target. Why would his own body not move as he wanted it to? Shuichi immediately slammed his fist into his thigh.

default.p.test-38-p3.vietnamese:
(Minosuke is running a shop that sells oil lamps.)

Before long, Minosuke bent down and picked up a stone from the ground. Then he aimed at the brightest oil lamp and threw it with all his might. There was a loud crash, and one of the large flames went out. 「Your time has passed. Society has progressed」—Minosuke said. Then he picked up another stone. The second-largest lamp made a loud crash and went out. 「Society has progressed. The age of electricity has arrived.」

When he smashed the third lamp, for some reason tears welled up in Minosuke's eyes, and he could no longer bring himself to aim at the lamps.

In this way, Minosuke gave up the business he had been running until then. After that, he moved to town and started a new business. He became a bookseller (opened a bookstore).

(Note 1) Lamp: a container for oil that is burned to provide light.

(Note 2) The times: the era

default.p.test-39-p1.vietnamese:
「So, do you know what this faint white streak, which people once called a river or the trace of flowing milk, really is?」 The teacher pointed to the hazy white band resembling the Milky Way (Note 2), flowing from top to bottom across the large black star chart hanging on the blackboard, and asked the entire class.

Campanella raised his hand. Then four or five other students raised theirs as well. Giovanni was about to raise his hand too, but quickly stopped. He had indeed read somewhere in a magazine that all of it consisted of stars, but lately Giovanni seemed sleepy in class every day. He had neither time to read nor any books to read, so he felt as if he did not really understand anything.

However, the teacher quickly noticed what he had done.

「Giovanni. You know the correct answer, don't you?」

Giovanni stood up energetically, but once he was standing, he could no longer explain it clearly. Zanelli turned around from the row in front, looked at Giovanni, and snickered. Giovanni was so embarrassed that his face turned bright red. The teacher continued:

「If you observe the Milky Way very carefully with a large telescope, what is the Milky Way, broadly speaking?」

Giovanni still thought that it was, as expected, stars, but this time he could not answer immediately either.

（Note 1）けぶった: a hazy state, appearing as though covered by smoke

（Note 2）銀河帯: the Milky Way

default.p.test-39-p2.vietnamese:
「You kids—surely you know, don’t you?」

「Know what?」

My aunt looked back at the screen and watched the action on the sumo ring intently for a while before turning to look at us again.

「Actually, your mother carefully considered every front and back side of each leaf when arranging flowers. Satoko-chan used to be an ikebana teacher, you know」

As she spoke, my aunt reached for the box of cookies, looked at the screen, and exclaimed, "Oh, dear!" The match ended so quickly. Then she stood up and turned off the television at the power switch. Even though we had told her many times that using the main power switch would make the remote control unusable, she kept doing the same thing.

According to my aunt, after returning to the sofa, Mother had diligently studied both flower arrangement and tea ceremony when she was young, and she had been exceptionally skilled at both.

「She had reached a very high level. And it wasn’t just flower arrangement—Satoko-chan could do everything」

「Really?」

Nanaha and I exclaimed at the same time. My aunt laughed and said, "Well, well."

「You two really are in perfect sync」

I nodded vaguely. Although Nanaha and I had uttered the same phrase, our feelings were very different. Nanaha was probably looking at Mother with greater admiration. I was also seeing Mother in a new light, but I was following a completely opposite line of thought from Nanaha. I felt slightly disappointed. I was not disappointed in Mother, but perhaps in the image of my own future self appearing in the past tense through Mother. My aunt stared into Nanaha’s eyes as Nanaha eagerly waited to hear more, then said:

「Your mother was really cool back then」

Nanaha smiled with delight. As expected, I was still bothered by the past tense—by the words "was really cool."

(Note 1) 土俵の成り行き: the outcome of a sumo match

(Note 2) お花のお師匠さん: a teacher of traditional Japanese ikebana

(Note 3) リモコン: a remote-control device for operating equipment from nearby

(Note 4 (Note 5)) 華道, 茶道: traditional Japanese rules and etiquette for flower arrangement (= ikebana) and tea ceremony

(Note 6) 曖昧: unclear, vague

default.p.test-4-p1.vietnamese:
「In the near future, half of today's occupations will be replaced by AI」. Hearing this, many people may feel anxious. They may worry, 「Will I lose my job?」 or 「Will this profession disappear?」. So, are there occupations that AI cannot replace? What kind of occupations will not be replaced by AI?

What about occupations in the arts, for example? Recently, we have heard that AI has painted pictures imitating the famous painter Rembrandt, conducted symphony orchestras, and written a novel that passed the preliminary selection for a literary award. If we think about it this way, will the arts also be replaced by AI? I do not think so. Even AI may be able to analyze a famous painter and apply colors to a canvas. Moreover, it may be possible to analyze popular music and create songs or lyrics that appeal to the general public. However, ②. People are moved by art when they sense the soul of the artist who created the work. Because they sense a 「human being」 there—the various emotions of life, such as joy, anger, love, and sorrow—they are deeply moved and captivated by art. In other words, this is precisely what can be called 「human value」, which AI cannot replace.

(Note 1) AI: Artificial intelligence

(Note 2) Imitating Rembrandt: Reproducing the expressive style of the painter Rembrandt (Rembrandt)

(Note 3) Appealing to the general public: Liked by many people

(Note 4) Joy, anger, love, and sorrow: The diverse emotions of human beings, such as happiness, anger, sadness, and delight

default.p.test-40-p1.vietnamese:
In psychology, there is a concept called the “Johari Window.” It is a model that divides the self into four areas: “the self known both to oneself and to others,” “the self known to oneself but not shown to others,” “the self not recognized by oneself but seen by others,” and “the self known neither to oneself nor to others,” representing them as window panes.

Among these, expanding the window of “the self known both to oneself and to others”—in other words, opening oneself up to others and shrinking the remaining three windows—is considered helpful for building good relationships with the people around us.

Has anyone ever pointed out a flaw in you? If someone points out that you unintentionally made them uncomfortable without realizing it, you probably would not feel very good. However, it is also a good opportunity to become aware of “the self not recognized by oneself but seen by others” and make that window smaller. By taking criticism of your flaws seriously, you can correct them and help yourself grow.

（Note 1）Psychology: the field of study that examines changes in the human mind.

default.p.test-40-p2.outline.0.note: Gives various reasons and purposes for learning a foreign language, such as traveling, living abroad, working, and watching films.
default.p.test-40-p2.outline.1.label: The nature of language and communication
default.p.test-40-p2.outline.1.note: Language is a means of communication, but simply memorizing vocabulary and grammar is not enough.
default.p.test-40-p2.outline.2.label: Real communication is closely connected with culture and history
default.p.test-40-p2.outline.2.note: The passage gives examples of differences in cultural expression and points out that genuine communication requires understanding the country’s culture and history as well (evidence for question 2).
default.p.test-40-p2.outline.3.label: Conclusion: A foreign language is a means, not an end
default.p.test-40-p2.outline.3.note: Concludes that learning a foreign language is only a means of communicating with and understanding people, with an accompanying explanation of the annotation.
default.p.test-40-p2.vietnamese:
What is the purpose of learning a foreign language? Being able to communicate directly with people from other countries is certainly appealing. Some people may need a foreign language when traveling or living abroad, or may have to learn one because their work requires it. Others may want to understand directly what their favorite film actors are saying.

Language is a means of communication: conveying what we want to say and understanding what the other person is saying. This is fundamental. However, memorizing vocabulary and grammar does not automatically enable us to communicate.

For example, when one unpleasant thing after another happens in a single day, one language may use the expression, "Today is the worst day of my life," while another may say, "Today is terribly unlucky." Such expressions are based on the culture of each language. If we merely replace words in one language with words in another, a smartphone's translation function would already be sufficient. True communication, however, is not simply a matter of becoming able to use a foreign language. It is created only after we understand the country, including its culture and history. Nevertheless, even when languages differ, if we have the intention of conveying something to the other person and a strong desire to do so, we can sometimes surprisingly communicate through facial expressions, gestures, and body movements.

Learning a foreign language is only a means, not the goal.

(Note 1) 事足りる: To be sufficient; to meet the need fully.

(Note 2) 身振り手振り: Gestures and body movements; movements of the hands and body.

default.p.test-40-p3.vietnamese:
Many different kinds of living organisms coexist on the Earth where we live. From microorganisms invisible to the naked eye to large animals, they are all connected and interact with one another to form ecosystems. However, as the human population has grown and human activity has intensified, the environment has changed, and some organisms are now facing the threat of extinction. It is important for us to think about such organisms whose numbers are declining and to maintain the biodiversity of their habitats.

Why, then, is maintaining biodiversity necessary?

In an ecosystem made up of only a few species, if one species becomes extinct, the species that feeds on it will also become extinct. As a result, the entire ecosystem will eventually be greatly affected. In an ecosystem made up of many species, however, relationships such as eating and being eaten are complex, so the extinction of one species will not affect the entire environment. As long as humans are also living organisms dependent on the connections called ecosystems, maintaining biodiversity is what stabilizes the Earth’s environment and preserves a livable Earth for humanity.

（Note 1）Ecosystem: All the living organisms in a particular area and their surrounding environment, regarded as one interconnected whole.

（Note 2）Facing the threat of: Being in a dangerous situation that is approaching immediately.

default.p.test-41-p1.vietnamese:
Many people have probably heard the term "lifestyle-related diseases." It refers to illnesses such as high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, and diabetes, which result from changes in eating habits and a lack of exercise. These diseases do not necessarily cause pain or clear symptoms, so they are difficult for sufferers to notice themselves. While thinking things like "I've been getting tired easily lately" or "I don't have much appetite," their health may already be deteriorating, and in many cases the disease has progressed severely by the time they visit a hospital.

A regular health checkup is a good opportunity to find out what condition your body is currently in. By having a checkup and recognizing which aspects of our own lifestyle are problematic, we can improve our habits and prevent illness.

Furthermore, health checkups can detect diseases before symptoms that we can notice ourselves appear. If diseases that we would not recognize on our own are found early, we can stop them from becoming serious and may also be able to treat them. Even with cancer, some cases can be cured if it is detected early and treatment begins promptly. This reduces the burden both physically and financially.

Be aware that you must protect your own health yourself, and have regular health checkups. It is also important to pay attention to your health every day, for example by watching what you eat and exercising moderately.

(Note 1) High blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, and diabetes: Diseases involving blood pressure and the components of the blood.

(Note 2) Symptom: A condition caused by an illness.

(Note 3) Cancer: A disease caused by cancer cells.

default.p.test-41-p2.vietnamese:
When we happen to argue with friends, fail at work, or find that nothing goes smoothly, there may be times when we feel discouraged and depressed and think, 「I'm really useless」. However, even in the same circumstances, our view of events changes depending on our mental state and how we interpret them.

To make this possible, it is also effective to make an effort to change the perspective from which we observe ourselves. We tend to view everything from the same fixed perspective, and as a result, our thinking easily falls into a one-pattern, stereotyped way of thinking. We ourselves are often completely unaware of this.

Moreover, when it comes to aspects in which we lack confidence or feel inferior, we are even more likely to interpret things negatively. We may become anxious, thinking, for example, 「The person who just walked past kept staring at me, and it feels as though the person next to them was laughing at me. Could my clothes look strange?」, or make assumptions such as 「My boss keeps assigning all the work to me. Does my boss hate me?」.

However, this may also stem from our own lack of confidence. Why not try interpreting things in a way such as 「Perhaps they are complimenting me on how nice my outfit looks」 or 「My boss assigned this to me because they value my ability to work」? Simply making an effort to direct our thoughts positively can reduce emotional distress and recharge our spirits.

(Endnote 1) One-pattern: always becoming stereotyped and following the same pattern

(Endnote 2) Complex: here, a feeling of being inferior or less capable than others

(Endnote 3) Negative: denying or pessimistic in nature

(Endnote 4) Positive: affirming or optimistic in nature

default.p.test-42-p1.vietnamese:
The rice variety that immediately comes to mind when people talk about rice—the staple food of the Japanese—is 「Koshihikari」. Koshihikari ranks first in planted area (Note 1), but astonishingly, it has continuously held the number-one position for several decades. Moreover, varieties grown in large quantities after Koshihikari, such as 「Hitomebore」 and 「Akitakomachi」, are all descendants of Koshihikari. Japanese people grow almost exclusively Koshihikari or varieties that inherit its characteristics. Is this really normal? Growing only varieties with similar characteristics is extremely dangerous. When a disease breaks out, all varieties with the same characteristics will be infected. If we continue growing only similar varieties, there is a risk that, in the worst case, they could all be wiped out. I think that, to minimize this risk, we should promote the development of rice varieties and grow a wide range of varieties in different regions.

(Note 1) Planted area: the area in which a rice variety is cultivated

default.p.test-42-p2.vietnamese:
―― I understand.

At work, my boss keeps pushing all the tasks onto me, while the people around me pretend not to notice. There are so many things I want to do and learn outside of work, but I do not even have time for them. Even though I had a date today, I had to finish the extra work before rushing out of the office, so I did not even have time to touch up my makeup……

The woman standing in front of her boyfriend says these things in a rapid, nonstop stream. He listens and nods, and when there is a brief pause in her story, he gently embraces her and says one sentence: "I understand."

It is certainly a scene that seems to exist only in movies or television dramas, but perhaps there is no woman who would not long for such a situation. Put another way, this means that in everyday life, almost no one treats us in that way.

Judging from the stories told by people I have met in the clinic, having a spouse or partner "listen while nodding" to one's story could still be considered a good outcome. Most of the time, when people say things like "Something awful happened to me today," their partner either interrupts with "I'm exhausted too, you know," or responds absentmindedly while staring at their phone. Aren't those usually the only two possibilities?

Another story I often hear at the clinic is that, when the other person is somewhat more sincere, they may listen temporarily but then argue against the story or add their own explanations. For example, to a partner telling the story from the opening, they might say:

"No, but are you really the only one being overloaded with work? Isn't it impossible to compare your workload with other people's objectively? Besides, I think time depends on how skillfully each person arranges things—you can create as much of it as you want. If you simply finished your lunch break ten minutes earlier and started working, couldn't you create much more free time?"

Those words may indeed be logically valid, but people who share a story like "This happened today" with a spouse or partner they trust do not want to hear criticism or lectures. Especially when the story is not cheerful but concerns dissatisfaction, anger, anxiety, or complaining, isn't the first thing they want to hear simply: "I understand"?

（Note 1）上の空 (absent-minded): being preoccupied with something else and unable to focus attention on the present matter.

（Note 2）冒頭 (opening): the beginning.

default.p.test-43-p1.outline.0.label: The essence of “knowing what is enough” (知足)
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.0.note: The passage begins by emphasizing the need to “know what is enough” today and clarifies Laozi’s idea of “knowing sufficiency”: it does not mean suppressing desire, but living independently without being controlled by external things.
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.1.label: Taking back control of one's life
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.1.note: The passage analyzes the harm of relentlessly pursuing external values and the importance of controlling one’s own life and recognizing intrinsic beauty. It provides evidence for the first part of Question 1.
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.2.label: Finding joy in the present
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.2.note: Points out the endless cycle of pursuing what one lacks and asserts that people who know how to be content can find joy in what they already have. This contains the basis for the latter part of Question 1.
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.3.label: Knowing when enough is enough as the foundation for effort and self-improvement
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.3.note: Clarifies the point: “knowing when enough is enough” does not mean settling for stagnation, but is a necessary foundation and stepping stone for cultivating effort and ambition.
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.4.label: Notes on classical vocabulary
default.p.test-43-p1.outline.4.note: Explanations of the philosophical terms from Laozi appearing in the reading passage.
default.p.test-43-p1.vietnamese:
More than two thousand years have passed since Laozi expounded the Way, but perhaps there has never been an era in which knowing when enough is enough has been as difficult and as necessary as it is today.

The “knowing enough” that Laozi spoke of does not simply mean putting up with things or restraining one's desires. Do not allow yourself to be controlled by external things such as material possessions, money, fame, status, or other people's opinions. I believe he was advising us to live autonomously and become more satisfied with ourselves.

External values are also indispensable to human beings, but the more we seek them outside ourselves and demand them from others, the more our lives are controlled by them, and the less we remain masters of ourselves. Therefore, put an end yourself to the mind that unconsciously keeps demanding too much by thinking: having enough to live is sufficient; anything beyond that is unnecessary. Try decisively to give up spending time and energy busily enhancing your external value or worrying about how others judge you.

Of course, we cannot give everything up completely, but what matters is making the effort to let go and gradually take control of our lives back into our own hands. As we do so, our eyes will begin to turn toward the radiant beauty inherent in life itself—something completely unrelated to possessions or status. We will realize that this radiance also exists within us and gradually feel that our present selves, just as we are, are not bad at all.

Even if we obtain the things that are said to make us happy or the things we think we lack, we will simply want something else next. As long as we continue doing this, happiness will always remain somewhere a little farther ahead. However, once you know when enough is enough, you will no longer be like a horse tirelessly chasing the carrot dangling in front of its nose. You will surely be able to actively find abundant joy in what you already have in your hands at the present moment.

Although saying that knowing enough is important, this does not mean doing nothing and complacently remaining stuck in the current situation. After the phrase “The one who knows enough is rich,” Laozi continued with “The one who strives to act has determination.” By saying that the person who strives to put things into practice is a person of determination, he was advising us to encourage ourselves, maintain our resolve, and continue making an effort.

A progressive spirit and effort are also indispensable keys to living happily. To make use of that key, I believe that, as a first step and foundation, we must first engrave the two words “knowing enough” deeply in our hearts.

(Note 1) Laozi expounding the Way: Laozi, an ancient Chinese thinker, discussing the ideals of human beings.

(Note 2) Knowing enough (= 知足): Knowing how to be content and satisfied.

(Note 3) 知足者富: Knowing how to be content is true wealth.

(Note 4) 強行者有志: A person who strives to put things into practice is a person with a goal and determination.
